text:
91
Durchläuchtigſter Fürſt.
Gnädigster Herr.
Ew Hochfürstlichen Durchlaucht danke ich
unterthänigst, für die Aufschluße, die
Höchstdieselben in der Güther-Vertauschungs
Angelegenheit nur zu ertheilen geruhet
haben. Dabey ist es mir eine unendliche
Freude, daß Sr. Majestät die angetragenen
weitere Untersuchung verfügt haben,
und versicher ich unterthänigst, daß ich im
weitern Verfolg dieser Angelegenheit
meine Pflichten eben so gewißenhaft als
bisher beobachten, also auch keinen Auswegen
unbringt laßen werde, der die Wünsche
Ew Hochfürstlichen Durchlaucht, die Geneigs
heit meines Herrn ihnen entgegen zu
kommen und des Interesse des Staats mit
einander zu vereinigen im Stande
seyn wird. Dieser Versicherung füge
ich die Betheuerung der unbegrenz¬
testen Ehrerbietigkeit hinzu, womit
ich lebenslang verharre
Ew Hochfürstlichen Durchlaucht
Berlin
den 17ten Xbr.
1798.
unterthänigster Diener
Beyme

translation.en:
91

Most Serene Prince.

Most gracious Lord.

To Your Most Serene Highness I return my most humble thanks for the explanations which Your Highness has been pleased only to impart in the matter of the exchange of estates. It is withal an infinite joy to me that His Majesty has ordered the further investigation that was proposed, and I most humbly assure that in the further prosecution of this matter I shall observe my duties just as conscientiously as heretofore, and accordingly shall leave no expedients [uncertain: unbringt] which may be capable of reconciling the wishes of Your Most Serene Highness, the inclination of my Lord to meet them, and the interest of the state with

one another. To this assurance I add the protestation of the most unbounded reverence, wherewith I remain lifelong Your Most Serene Highness's Berlin

the 17th of December

1798.

most humble and obedient servant Beyme

text_english:
91

Most Serene Prince.

Most gracious Lord.

To Your Most Serene Highness I return my most humble thanks for the explanations which Your Highness has been pleased only to impart in the matter of the exchange of estates. It is withal an infinite joy to me that His Majesty has ordered the further investigation that was proposed, and I most humbly assure that in the further prosecution of this matter I shall observe my duties just as conscientiously as heretofore, and accordingly shall leave no expedients [uncertain: unbringt] which may be capable of reconciling the wishes of Your Most Serene Highness, the inclination of my Lord to meet them, and the interest of the state with

one another. To this assurance I add the protestation of the most unbounded reverence, wherewith I remain lifelong Your Most Serene Highness's Berlin

the 17th of December

1798.

most humble and obedient servant Beyme
summary_en: Beyme thanks the Prince for the information he has given in the matter of the exchange of estates. He says he is glad that the King has ordered a further investigation, and he gives his assurance that he will continue to carry out his duties conscientiously. In doing so he intends to reconcile the Prince's wishes, his own master's readiness to accommodate him, and the interest of the state.
summary_de: Beyme dankt dem Fürsten für die Aufschlüsse in der Güter-Vertauschungs-Angelegenheit. Er freut sich, dass der König eine weitere Untersuchung verfügt hat, und versichert, er werde seine Pflichten weiter gewissenhaft erfüllen. Dabei will er die Wünsche des Fürsten, die Bereitschaft seines Herrn, ihm entgegenzukommen, und das Interesse des Staates miteinander vereinigen.

reading.notes: Beyme (Berlin) replies to the Prince: thanks him for explanations about the estate-exchange matter (Güther-Vertauschungs Angelegenheit), is glad the King has ordered a further investigation, and promises to keep doing his duty as conscientiously as before, looking for a way to bring together the Prince's wishes, his master's willingness to accommodate him, and the interest of the state. Short courtesy letter. A few words are garbled: "Er" on line 4 (a formula error), "nur" on line 7, "unbringt" on line 15, "des Interesse" on line 18.
